text:
maria (sre): Quick broadcast: follow-up from last night's EU routing throttling incident and a short policy update we agreed on in the post-incident sync. Thread for owners + next steps.

sre-bot: Alert: routing-proxy-eu-west high queue depth detected 2026-03-23T22:12Z -> automatic model-fallback executed to quant-1 variant.

maria (sre): Short recap: node reboot wave triggered kube-proxy flaps -> control-plane admission spiked -> our rate limiter started shedding then tripped fallback at 22:13. Mitigations restored steady state by 22:35.

tony (sre): Measured impact: p99 upstream latency +170ms, error rate rose to 0.8% for ~18m. No customer data loss. Logged traces show slow connection churn into router.

eli (sre): Root cause hypothesis: simultaneous kubelet restarts + router autoscaler rapid scale-in. Autoscaler cooldown allowed 3 nodes to reboot in quick succession.

kai (runtime): Temporary mitigations we pushed: reduce router-scale-in aggressiveness, enable shorter kv-cache TTL during control-plane pressure, and lower soft-preempt aggressiveness on one canary pool. Rolled 22:20-22:30.

sam (prod): Some customers on EU saw slight generation quality drift after fallback. Support logged ~6 tickets noting punctuation differences. Should product notify proactively?

maria (sre): Decision: we need an explicit policy for automated fallbacks. Draft below is effective immediately unless legal/product override.

maria (sre): New fallback classification policy:
- "Controlled fallback": automatic switch to lower-footprint model variants triggered by routing/infra pressure with preserved response completeness. Treated separately from outages.
- Paging rules: do NOT page SRE on controlled fallbacks if user-visible error-rate <1% and duration <15min.
- Post-incident: any controlled fallback lasting >15min leads to a 72h corrective action ticket + postmortem summary.
- Customer comms: for any fallback that changes model family or quantization (may alter output), product must be notified within 30 minutes so a customer-facing note can be issued.
- Dedicated customers: auto-fallbacks are disabled by default. Any fallback for dedicated requires account + security gate approval.

tony (sre): Technical controls we will implement:
- Circuit-breaker: per-AZ inflight-control-plane limit (5000) reject policy to avoid control-loop amplification. Owner: tony.
- Router ASG cooldown: raise scale-in cooldown from 45s -> 120s for router ASG. Owner: kai.
- Synthetic: weekly node-reboot + soft-preempt synthetic test to run in staging and one canary region. Owner: eli.

sam (prod): I'll prepare the 30-minute notification template and a short FAQ about what customers can expect when we fall back to quantized models. Will coordinate with support.

support-oncall: Please confirm whether support should auto-send the template when we hit a fallback event or wait for product to review each time.

maria (sre): For now: support should hold until product posts the reviewed template. After that point support can send pre-approved templates for controlled fallbacks.

eli (sre): I'll open GH issues for the circuit-breaker and synthetic test and add owners/due dates. Link will be posted here once created.

tony (sre): I'll draft the PR for the breaker rule and schedule a small canary rollout window next week.

kai (runtime): I'll update the ASG config and add the cooldown change to the infra changelog.

sre-bot: Scheduled: canary for circuit-breaker rule 2026-03-26T01:00Z.

maria (sre): Thanks everyone. We'll add the policy to the Reliability Playbook and update the alerting runbook to reflect the new non-paging thresholds for controlled fallbacks. Post the playbook link here when merged. Closing thread. :thumbsup:
